narrative:
The model estimates a 55% chance that you will leave your job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This prediction is driven primarily by three key factors about your background and current role.

Your relatively short overall career experience of just 1-5 years was the strongest factor pulling the prediction toward leaving. Most employees the model expects to stay have similar short tenures, but the pattern in the data shows that limited total experience often signals higher turnover risk in this sector.

The second most influential factor was that you have received other job offers while working here. Having external opportunities strongly pushes the prediction toward leaving, as it suggests you have realistic alternatives that many employees predicted to stay do not possess.

Third, working in the “other” sector (rather than medical or education) also nudged the model toward expecting you to leave. Only about 22% of employees the model thinks will stay work in this broader category, making it a less stable group in the eyes of the model.

Taken together, your limited experience, external opportunities, and sector create a profile the model associates with higher turnover. The organization should discuss retention measures with you, such as clearer promotion paths or stronger recognition of your contributions. You may want to reflect on whether your current role still aligns with your longer-term goals.
